about.title: Los Gatos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Los Gatos may feel like a quieter corner of Santa Clara County, but its mix of retail corridors, construction along Los Gatos Boulevard and Blossom Hill Road, and delivery traffic near SR-17 and SR-85 means workplace injuries still happen here — falls, vehicle collisions on the job, equipment accidents, and repetitive strain from warehouse or service work. California workers' compensation typically covers medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault, but it's usually the only remedy against your own employer. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim worth exploring. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we simply connect injured workers in Los Gatos with an independent attorney who can review the facts, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand what deadlines apply. There's no cost to start the conversation, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Move Forward

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: California law generally makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held separately accountable.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You typically need to notify your employer of a workplace injury within 30 days, so acting promptly helps protect your ability to pursue benefits.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish or fire you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can explain what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near SR-85 in Los Gatos. Is that a workers' comp case or something else?
items.answer: It could be both. Workers' compensation may cover your medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against them. An independent attorney can look at the details and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer?
items.answer: In California, you generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. Waiting too long can complicate your claim, so it's worth reporting as soon as you're able.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options.
